notes.content: The continuation discusses compatibility as an additional relation on the collection M beyond its two order relations. It says that, morally and at least in the moderate case, these three relations suffice to recover the atelier up to unique isomorphism. It then proposes parallel uprights for disjunction and two graphical alternatives for compatibility, noting a tradeoff between speed of writing and combinatorial suggestiveness. The last paragraph turns to the refinement relation, calls it more delicate and particularly characteristic of the Algèbre des figures, and begins to refer to examples and their axioms; the sentence continues beyond this scan.
math_reading_decisions: The collection letter M is transcribed calligraphically; both relation indices are centered beneath the signs.
The ordinary operands F and G remain distinct from the family F in the final paragraph. The latter retains the cal/frak alphabet uncertainty.
The live divided-diamond compatibility sign and the circled alternative are reproduced with inline TikZ. The latter has crossed zigzags, not horizontal hourglass caps.

The old relation in the final paragraph is visually read as deleted ll, followed by live preccurlyeq; the live word raffinement is preserved without attempting to reconcile terminology on unseen pages.
The dark sign in the NB has uncertain live/deleted state, shown in the text itself. No mathematical expectation decides it.
The NB has an opening parenthesis and no visible closing parenthesis. The page ends mid-clause; no continuation was supplied from another scan.
